back: Quad-core Cortex A53 processor, approximately 1.2 GHz.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: Which common Raspberry Pi variant lacks built-in Ethernet and WiFi?
back: Raspberry Pi Zero.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What is the primary video output port on a Raspberry Pi?
back: HDMI port.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What do the initials GPIO stand for in the context of Raspberry Pi?
back: General Purpose Input Output pins.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: How many GPIO pins are typically available on a Raspberry Pi?
back: 40 GPIO pins.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What is the main function of the memory card in a Raspberry Pi?
back: It actually holds the OS (Operating System) of the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: Name three types of physical ports found on a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B.
back: HDMI port, USB ports, Ethernet port, Power adapter port, Sound card output. (Any three)

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What dual function can Raspberry Pi GPIO pins serve?
back: They can act as both digital output and digital input.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What are the basic components required for the initial setup of a Raspberry Pi?
back: External monitor, HDMI cable, keyboard and mouse, 5V adapter, LAN cable, and a memory card with the OS.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: Name two official operating system distributions for Raspberry Pi.
back: Raspbian and NOOBS.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What software is recommended for writing a Raspbian image onto an SD card on a Windows system?
back: Win32 Disk Imager.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What is the default username and password for remotely logging into a Raspberry Pi system?
back: Username: pi, Password: raspberry.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What command is used to check the IP address of the Raspberry Pi from its terminal?
back: ip config.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What is the purpose of the 'Expand File System' option in the Raspberry Pi configuration?
back: To expand the compressed OS image to cover the maximum capacity of the memory card, providing more space.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What does SSH stand for, and why is it enabled on Raspberry Pi?
back: Secure Shell login; it allows remote access to the Raspberry Pi over the network from any remote PC.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: Name three programming languages that come pre-installed or are easily usable with Raspberry Pi.
back: Python (2/3), Scratch, BlueJ (Java), C, C++, Ruby. (Any three)

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: List two popular applications of Raspberry Pi in home environments.
back: Home automation systems and home monitoring (as a lightweight web server for IoT).

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: How can a Raspberry Pi be used as a lightweight web server for IoT?
back: It can act as a server for IoT devices to upload data, and can run various analytics on that data.

lectureTitle: Lecture 28: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- I
front: What is a key difference in power consumption between Raspberry Pi and Arduino?
back: Raspberry Pi has more power consumption compared to Arduino due to its higher computation capabilities.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the primary programming language used for integrating sensors and devices with Raspberry Pi in this lecture?
back: Python

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the purpose of using SSH with Raspberry Pi?
back: To execute and run various programs remotely from any PC.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the easier way to transfer files to/from Raspberry Pi compared to SSH?
back: Using an FTP client.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: Name a preferred FTP client mentioned for file transfer with Raspberry Pi.
back: FileZilla

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: In FileZilla, what do the left-hand and right-hand panels generally show?
back: Left-hand panel shows local PC contents, right-hand panel shows remote PC contents.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the default port used for FTP connections to Raspberry Pi?
back: Port 22

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is a common practice for programming larger projects on Raspberry Pi to avoid cumbersome direct programming?
back: Program everything on a local PC, then transfer the eventual files into the Raspberry Pi for minor configurations.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: List the basic hardware requirements for a blinking LED project with Raspberry Pi.
back: Raspberry Pi (connected to network), LED, 100 ohm resistor, breadboard, and a few jumper cables.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: How is the Pi Camera connected to the Raspberry Pi, specifically regarding the ribbon wire orientation?
back: The blue side of the ribbon wire should be pointed towards the Ethernet port.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: How do you identify the positive and negative terminals of a basic LED?
back: The larger one is the positive terminal, and the smaller one is the negative terminal.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What two Python libraries are required for connecting to GPIO terminals for the blinking LED project?
back: The `python-dev` library and the `python-rpi.gpio` library.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What command is used to install the `python-dev` library on Raspberry Pi?
back: `sudo apt-get install python-dev`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What command is used to install the `python-rpi.gpio` library on Raspberry Pi?
back: `sudo apt-get install python-rpi.gpio`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What command is used to open or create a Python file for editing in the terminal on Raspberry Pi?
back: `sudo nano filename.py` (e.g., `sudo nano led_blink.py`)

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: How do you save and exit the `nano` editor after writing code?
back: Press `Control + O` to write the code, then `Control + X` to exit.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What Python line imports the RPi.GPIO library?
back: `import RPi.GPIO as GPIO`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What Python line imports the time library for delay functions?
back: `import time`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: How is the GPIO mode set to use board numbering in Python?
back: `GPIO.setmode(GPIO.BOARD)`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: How do you set up GPIO pin 11 as an output pin in Python?
back: `GPIO.setup(11, GPIO.OUT)`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: How do you send a high bit (turn on) to GPIO pin 11 in Python?
back: `GPIO.output(11, True)`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: How do you send a low bit (turn off) to GPIO pin 11 in Python?
back: `GPIO.output(11, False)`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What Python function is used to introduce a delay (e.g., for 1 second)?
back: `time.sleep(1)`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the purpose of `GPIO.cleanup()` at the end of a GPIO script?
back: To release the GPIO pins.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: How do you run a Python script named `pi_led_blink.py` from the terminal on Raspberry Pi?
back: `python pi_led_blink.py`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What dedicated slot on the Raspberry Pi is used for connecting the Pi Camera?
back: CSI slot

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: Where is the CSI slot for the Pi Camera located on the Raspberry Pi?
back: Between the Ethernet port and the HDMI port.

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What command is used in the terminal to enable the camera option on Raspberry Pi?
back: `sudo raspi-config`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What terminal command is used to capture an image directly from the Pi Camera and save it as `image.jpeg`?
back: `raspistill -o image.jpeg`

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What Python library is needed to integrate the Pi Camera with Python?
back: `picamera` (installed via `python-picamera`)

lectureTitle: Lecture 29: Introduction to Raspberry Pi- II
front: What are two key advantages of Raspberry Pi compared to regular computers mentioned in the lecture?
back: It is very low on power requirements and quite cheap.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What are the three main aspects of IoT implementation with Raspberry Pi covered in this lecture series?
back: Integrating sensors, disseminating data (e.g., UDP to remote server), and visualizing data at the server.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What is the primary function of a sensor in an IoT system?
back: To convert a physical or measurable quantity into electrical signals.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: How do actuators function in an IoT system?
back: They are electromechanical devices that convert energy into motion, primarily used for providing control motion to other components.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: Name the key components required for the temperature-dependent auto-cooling system demonstrated.
back: DHT sensor, 4.7 kOhm resistor, relay, jumper wires, Raspberry Pi, and a mini fan.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: Describe the pin configuration of a DHT sensor.
back: Pin 1 for power (3.3-5V), Pin 2 for data, Pin 3 open, Pin 4 for ground.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: How is the DHT sensor connected to the Raspberry Pi's power and ground?
back: Pin 1 of DHT to 3.3V power supply of Raspberry Pi, Pin 4 of DHT to ground pin on the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: Which Raspberry Pi pin configuration mode does the DHT sensor follow for its data pin?
back: BCM configuration mode (e.g., Pin 7).

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What is a relay board, and what is its primary function?
back: An electromechanical switch used to control higher power devices with a low-power signal from the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: Name the three output terminals found on a sugar cube relay.
back: NO (Normally Open), Common, and NC (Normally Close).

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: How is the relay board connected to the Raspberry Pi for power and input signal?
back: VCC pin of relay to 5V supply of Raspberry Pi, Ground to Ground of Raspberry Pi, Input signal to Pin 11.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: Which Raspberry Pi pin configuration mode is used for connecting the relay's input signal?
back: Board mode (e.g., Pin 11).

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What is the first step to install the Adafruit DHT library on Raspberry Pi?
back: Use `git clone https://github.com/adafruit/Adafruit_Python_DHT.git` to download the repository.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: After cloning the Adafruit DHT repository, what command is used to navigate into the downloaded directory?
back: `cd Adafruit_Python_DHT`

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What command is used to install the Adafruit DHT Python library after navigating to its directory?
back: `sudo python setup.py install`

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What Python libraries are typically imported at the beginning of a DHT sensor program on Raspberry Pi?
back: `Rpi.GPIO`, `time`, and `Adafruit_DHT`.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: How do you initialize the DHT sensor type (e.g., AM2302) in the Adafruit DHT Python library?
back: `sensor = Adafruit_DHT.AM2302` (or `Adafruit_DHT.DHT22`, `Adafruit_DHT.DHT11`).

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What function is used to read humidity and temperature values from the DHT sensor using the Adafruit library?
back: `Adafruit_DHT.read_retry(sensor_type, pin_number)`

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: In the sample auto-cooling system, what was the basic decision-making logic for turning on the fan?
back: If the temperature is greater than 20 degrees Celsius, the fan is turned on.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: How is the mini fan connected to the relay for the auto-cooling system?
back: The NO (Normally Open) terminal of the relay connects to the positive terminal of the fan, and the Common terminal of the relay connects to the positive terminal of the battery.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What type of battery was used to power the mini fan in the demonstration?

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I

back: Data is read from the sensor, and the actuator is controlled according to that reading.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What advanced methods could replace the basic decision-making loop for controlling actuators?
back: Machine learning, statistical learning, or deep learning methods.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What protocol was mentioned for disseminating data through a network to a remote server?

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: How can you visually confirm that a relay has been activated during the demonstration?

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I
front: What is the primary goal of the 'temperature dependent auto cooling system' example?
back: To automatically turn on a fan when the temperature exceeds a certain threshold, providing an automated cooling solution.

lectureTitle: Lecture 30: Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- I

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the primary goal of the IoT implementation discussed in this lecture?
back: To integrate a DHT sensor with Raspberry Pi and include networking components for remote data logging using a client-server model.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What networking model is used for data transmission between Raspberry Pi and the remote desktop?
back: A client-server model using UDP (User Datagram Protocol) based sockets.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the basic aim of the Internet of Things regarding devices?
back: To create an interactive environment of networked devices, where more devices lead to a more intelligent and interactive system, maintaining performance.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Describe the system overview for the remote data logging demonstration.
back: A network of temperature and humidity sensors will be connected to Raspberry Pi, data from the sensors are read, sent to the server over the network, and the data is saved in the server.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: List the essential hardware requirements for this IoT implementation.
back: A Raspberry Pi, a DHT sensor, a 4.7 kOhm resistor, and jumper wires.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the purpose of the 4.7 kOhm resistor in the DHT sensor setup with Raspberry Pi?
back: It must be connected between the VCC and the data pin (pin one and two) of the DHT sensor.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Identify the function of the second pin of the DHT sensor when viewed from left to right with the grid side up.
back: The second pin is used for transmitting data.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: To which Raspberry Pi pin is the VCC pin of the DHT sensor connected?
back: The 3.3 volt pin of the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Which Raspberry Pi pin (in BCM mode) is connected to the data pin (pin 2) of the DHT sensor?
back: Pin 11 of the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: To which Raspberry Pi pin is the ground pin (pin 4) of the DHT sensor connected?
back: The ground pin of the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What GPIO mode must be used for the DHT sensor connection in this setup?
back: The board configuration for this DHT sensor must be in BCM mode, not in board mode.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Which Python library is used to integrate the DHT22 sensor with Raspberry Pi?
back: The Adafruit_DHT library, provided by Adafruit which supplies the DHT22 sensor.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What specific function from the Adafruit_DHT library is used to read data from the sensor?
back: The `adafruit_dht.read_retry` function.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the general purpose of sockets in network communication?
back: Sockets generally create a two-way communication between two nodes in a network, one node termed as the server and the other as the client.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What Python function is used to create a socket?
back: The `socket.socket` function.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Name the three arguments of the `socket.socket()` function.
back: Socket family, socket type, and protocol (which is by default zero).

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Which socket family is typically used for general-purpose internet protocols?
back: `AF_INET` (Internet protocols).

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Which socket type is used for UDP-based communication (datagrams)?
back: `SOCK_DGRAM` (socket datagram).

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is a critical requirement for the server's IP address in a client-server model?
back: It is important that your server retain a singular IP address.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What information must each client be aware of to connect to the server?
back: Each and every client should be aware of the server's IP address as well as the port to which the client is going to connect.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What function is used by the server to associate its socket with a specific host and port?
back: The server binds to the port by calling the host name as the first argument and the port number as the second argument.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: After binding, what function does a server call to wait for client connections?
back: The server starts its listening function which waits for a client to connect to it.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What does the `accept()` function return when a client connects to the server?
back: While a client has accepted the connection and connected to your server on that particular port, it will generate one address.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What function does the client use to establish a connection to the server's IP address and port?
back: The client uses `s.connect()` to connect to that particular IP address of that server on that particular port.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: In the UDP client code, which function is used to send data to the server address?
back: The data is transmitted over the socket to that particular server address using `sendto()`.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: In the UDP server code, which function is used to receive data and the sender's address?
back: The data and address will be received from the socket using `recvfrom()`.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: In what mode should the `data_log.txt` file be opened on the server to prevent overwriting previous data?
back: The file should be opened in append mode so that your data keeps on appending onto the same file again and again without overwriting the previous data.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: How is the humidity and temperature data formatted when sent from the client to the server?
back: The humidity and temperature data are formatted in the terms of a string (e.g., '74.3,25.7').

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What happens if the `data_log.txt` file does not exist when the server starts receiving data?
back: The server automatically creates another `data_log.txt` file.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Can multiple Raspberry Pis with sensors send data to a single server in this setup?
back: Yes, you can obviously include multiple Raspberry Pis and multiple sensors all sending data to this particular server or a single IP at the port.

back: Focusing more on the server side, that is once the data has arrived what exactly can be done with the data.

back: Creating an interactive environment using a network of connected devices and remote data logging.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What are the two main processing locations for data in the described IoT system?
back: The data may be processed on the client side as well as it may be processed on the server side itself.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the initial step in the system overview for this demonstration?
back: Start off with a network of temperature and humidity sensors connected with Raspberry Pi board.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III

back: Pin 2 of DHT is connected to Pin 11 of the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III

back: The Adafruit Python library for this DHT sensor.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: In the client-server architecture, which device acts as the client and which acts as the server?
back: We create a client server architecture and establish connection between one client device and a desktop which acts as the server device.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III

back: Successive data will be incoming into the server and get stored into a log file.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III

back: You need to filter the data to create a seamless and well structured database.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III

back: You have one two three then you have three two then you have five then abc then a blank since it has two fours so it includes a blank and then rt.

back: Both of these support a very powerful library called matplotlib.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III

back: This thing will help save you a lot of effort you don't need to individually code the clients.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the primary goal of Software Defined Networking (SDN)?
back: To transform or restructure the existing network infrastructure in an efficient manner.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is a key limitation of current day networks regarding network view?
back: Each switch does not have a global view of the network as a whole.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: In traditional networks, what happens if a switch goes down and there is no centralized control?
back: Finding an alternate route becomes a difficult task, as there is no centralized entity that can take care of it.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What are the three layers typically run on each switch in a traditional network?
back: Hardware, Operating System (OS), and Applications.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the core idea of SDN to overcome traditional network limitations?
back: To separate the application and operating system from the hardware.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: When did the idea of Software Defined Network (SDN) originate?
back: In 2008, with the OpenFlow project.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What was the name of the clean slate security architecture proposed by Stanford in 2006, which aimed for centralized security policies?
back: SANE.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the primary separation in the SDN architecture?
back: Separation of the data plane from the control plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What concept makes the separation of data and control planes possible in SDN?
back: Network Function Virtualization (NFV).

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Name the three different planes in the SDN architecture.
back: Data plane, control plane, and application plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the Northbound API in SDN?
back: The interface between the control plane and the application plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the Southbound API in SDN?
back: The interface between the forwarding (data plane) and the control plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Which protocol currently supports the Southbound API in SDN?
back: The OpenFlow protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is one of the key attributes of SDN regarding control logic?
back: The control logic is defined in a centralized manner.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: List two main challenges when implementing SDN in any network.
back: The Rule Placement Problem and the Controller Placement Problem.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: In SDN, what replaces routing tables in switches?
back: Flow tables.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Who defines the flow rules in SDN?
back: The centralized controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Where are flow tables stored in SDN switches?
back: In Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM).

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What are the characteristics of TCAM memory in SDN switches?
back: It is limited in size, very expensive, and allows for very fast processing.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What message does a switch send to the controller if no flow rule is present for a received request?
back: A 'Packet In' message.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the typical delay involved in placing a new rule in an SDN switch after a 'Packet In' message?
back: Three to five milliseconds.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is one challenge related to defining rules in SDN to minimize communication with the controller?
back: How to define the rules so that less number of 'Packet In' messages are sent to the controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Are the fields in an OpenFlow rule fixed or configurable?
back: The fields are fixed in a particular version of OpenFlow.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Describe the 'Hard Time Out' mechanism for flow rules in SDN.
back: All rules are deleted from the switch at a particular hard time, which can be done by resetting the switch for example.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Describe the 'Soft Time Out' mechanism for flow rules in SDN.
back: If no flow is received associated with a particular rule for a timeout interval of time, then this particular rule is deleted.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the fundamental difference between SDN and OpenFlow?
back: SDN is a technology or a concept, while OpenFlow is a protocol that is used to communicate between the data plane and control plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Name two popular open-source software implementations for OpenFlow switches.
back: Indigo, LINC, Pantou, or Open vSwitch.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: How does SDN help in minimizing operational costs and delays?
back: Operation cost and delay that are caused due to link failure can be significantly minimized using SDN.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What kind of memory is required for flow tables in SDN switches due to its speed?
back: Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM).

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the role of the centralized controller in SDN regarding flow rules?
back: The controller basically takes care of defining the flow rules based on which the streams of packets that are coming to each of the switches are processed.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the primary protocol used for the Southbound API communication in SDN?
back: OpenFlow protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the purpose of the Northbound API in SDN?
back: To communicate between the control layer and the application layer.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the 'east westbound API' concept in SDN?
back: This terminology comes into picture when we are talking about not a single controller but multiple controllers in the control layer.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the main function of controllers in SDN regarding flow rules?
back: Controllers define the flow rule according to the application specific requirements.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the typical delay for rule placement in a switch's flow table if not already existing?
back: About three to five milliseconds.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Why is minimizing rule placement delay important in SDN?
back: Otherwise, there will be a huge control overhead and control-linked delay.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Approximately how many requests can a single-threaded SDN controller handle per second?
back: Roughly about 200 requests in a second.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Describe the logical connection between an SDN controller and switches.
back: The controllers are logically connected to the switches in a one-hop distance, though physically they can be multiple hops away.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the basic characteristic of a 'flat architecture' for controller placement?
back: The switch and the controller are just logically one hop away. The switch sends a 'packet in' message to the controller if it doesn't have the flow rule.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: How does a 'hierarchical or tree architecture' arrange SDN controllers?
back: Controllers are placed hierarchically and connected to different switches in a tree-like fashion.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is a key characteristic of the 'ring architecture' for SDN controller placement?
back: Controllers are placed in a ring-like fashion, but a particular switch is connected to only one controller in this version.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the primary benefit of using a 'mesh architecture' for SDN controller placement?
back: It increases reliability and improves the fault tolerance of the network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Differentiate between 'distributed' and 'centralized' control decisions in SDN.
back: Distributed: Each sub-network is controlled by a different controller. Centralized: A network is controlled by a single controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the role of a 'backup controller' in SDN?
back: If the primary controller is down, the backup controller takes over, having a replica of the main controller to ensure uninterrupted network management.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: How can SDN enhance network security?
back: One can have enhanced level of security in the network by taking help of firewall, proxy, HTTP, and IDS.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the difference between a simulator and an emulator for SDN experimentation?
back: Simulators simulate the entire thing (packet flows, network, nodes). Emulators can be connected to the real network where real traffic can flow through.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Name a popular software used to create virtual networks with OpenFlow-enabled switches for SDN experimentation.
back: Mininet.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Which programming language does Mininet run on?
back: Python.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Name two popular controller configuration software used in SDN.
back: OpenDaylight and ONOS (also POX, NOX, Floodlight).

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the core motivation behind SDN?
back: To separate out the control logic from the data logic (data plane) to make the network efficient.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is a significant trade-off or challenge in SDN regarding control messages?
back: More number of control packets are going to flow through the network, increasing control message overhead.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What two particular issues does the performance of SDN primarily depend on?
back: The rule placement and the controller placement in the network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the goal of 'unified network management' in SDN?
back: To have an unified network management architectural framework using SDN while leveraging the global view of the network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the next topic to be discussed after this lecture on SDN?
back: How SDN can be used in IoT to make the Internet of Things efficient.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the role of the control plane in SDN?
back: The control logic is separated out to the control plane, which knows what has to be done with a particular flow and controls the overall flow in the network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What does a switch do when it receives a packet for which it doesn't have a flow rule?
back: It will send a 'packet in' message to the controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the main limitation of TCAM memory in the context of rule placement?
back: TCAM memory has limitations, which is a trade-off with delay in rule placement.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What kind of applications are now possible for SDN controllers beyond single-threaded ones?
back: Multi-threaded applications.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: In the context of SDN security, what is 'policy enforcement'?
back: Implementing a sequence of flow instructions for a policy chain, such as firewall, IDS, and proxy, to control traffic.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the primary difference between a remote controller and a local controller in SDN experimentation?
back: A remote controller can be situated in a remote place and communicated using IP address and port number, while a local controller is situated locally.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is one fundamental problem solved by integrating SDN into IoT?
back: Intelligent routing decision making.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How does SDN simplify information handling in IoT?
back: It simplifies information collection, analysis, and decision making.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What aspect of network management is improved by SDN in IoT?
back: Visibility of network resources and simplified network management based on user/application requirements.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What kind of analysis and decision-making is enhanced by SDN in IoT?
back: Intelligent traffic pattern analysis and coordinated decisions through the controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the overall impact of SDN on IoT network intelligence and efficiency?
back: More intelligence is infused into the network, improving its efficiency.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Name two tiers in the tiered segmentation of IoT networks.
back: Context-aware tier, Network tier, Application tier.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is a key challenge in programming traditional sensor nodes?
back: Real-time programming of each sensor node is typically not feasible.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Describe a characteristic of sensor node architectures from different vendors.
back: They follow vendor-specific architectures, lacking a single standard.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Why are heavy computations difficult to perform at traditional sensor nodes?
back: Sensor nodes are resource-constrained.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What limitation does limited memory impose on traditional sensor networks?
back: Cannot insert too many control programs.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the role of the SDN controller in an integrated IoT network?
back: It controls different aspects, improves orchestration, and enhances service logic.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How does SDN enable control over IoT end devices like sensors and actuators?
back: It provides centralized control.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the purpose of rule placement in an SDN-integrated IoT network, especially for access devices?
back: To handle issues like mobility and heterogeneity of end devices.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Where is traffic engineering typically managed in an SDN-integrated IoT network?
back: At the transport network level.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What functions are handled at the data center networks in an SDN-integrated IoT setup?
back: Flow classification and enhanced security.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the name of the protocol proposed by Low et al. in 2012 for sensor networks?
back: Sensor OpenFlow protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Name the two ways Sensor OpenFlow protocol handles data forwarding.
back: Value-centric data forwarding and ID-centric data forwarding.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Explain value-centric data forwarding in Sensor OpenFlow.
back: Data is forwarded if the sensor data exceeds a certain threshold value.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Explain ID-centric data forwarding in Sensor OpenFlow.
back: Data is forwarded based on the ID of the source node.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is a limitation of the Sensor OpenFlow protocol mentioned in the lecture?
back: Real-life implementation of such a method is not yet available.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the name of the protocol proposed by Bera et al. in 2016?
back: Soft WSN protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Name two major component solutions of the Soft WSN protocol.
back: Sensor device management and topology management.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What does sensor device management in Soft WSN comprise?
back: Sensor management, delay management, and active sleep management.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How did Soft WSN compare to traditional WSN in terms of packet delivery ratio?
back: It showed much improved packet delivery ratio.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How did Soft WSN affect the number of replicated data packets compared to traditional WSN?
back: It reduced the number of replicated data packets.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Why does Soft WSN have a higher number of control packets in the network?
back: Each time a node receives a new packet, it asks the controller for adequate forwarding logic.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the name of the SDN-integrated WSN platform published in INFOCOM 2015?
back: SDN-WISE.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What key feature does SDN-WISE propose for rule placement at sensor nodes?
back: A flow table for rule placement is available at the sensor nodes.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How can nodes be programmed in real-time in SDN-WISE?
back: Any programming language can be used through API to program the nodes in real time.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What protocol do sensor nodes typically run in the SDN-WISE work?
back: The 802.15.4 protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What are some key problems in traditional mobile wireless networks that SDN aims to address?
back: Scalability issues, static over-provisioning, inflexibility to manage mobile traffic, difficult management leading to misconfigurations, slow service introduction, and high CAPEX and OPEX.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What are the two important aspects of SDN that make it suitable for mobile networks?
back: The flow table paradigm (for end-to-end communication over multiple technologies) and logically centralized control (for efficient base station coordination and addressing intercellular interference).

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: How does SDN's flow table paradigm benefit mobile networks?
back: It is well-suited for end-to-end communication over multiple technologies such as Wi-Fi, 3G, and 4G.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What is the advantage of logically centralized control in SDN for mobile networks?
back: It is particularly useful for efficient base station coordination for addressing intercellular interference.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What is 'path management' in the context of SDN for mobile networks?
back: It concerns data that can be routed based on service requirements without depending on the core routing policies.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: How does network virtualization, enabled by SDN, help in mobile networks?
back: It abstracts physical resources from network services, providing seamless connectivity and service differentiation among users.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What problem does the SDWMN solution primarily aim to address in traditional mobile networks?
back: Interference from other nodes (e.g., between eNodeB signals).

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: Name the two key units in the SDWMN architecture responsible for interference management and mobile traffic management.
back: The Virtualized Radio Resource Management Unit (VRRMU) for interference and the Access Network Discovery and Service Function (ANDSF) unit for mobile traffic management.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What are the key benefits of adopting SDN in mobile networks?
back: Centralized control of devices manufactured by multiple vendors, higher rate of integration of new services, and abstracted network control and management.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: List some challenges for rule placement at access devices in SDN-based mobile networks.
back: General OpenFlow does not support wireless networks, users are mobile, the network is highly dynamic, frequent changes in rule placement are required, and there is a presence of heterogeneous devices.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: Describe the core concept of ODIN for rule placement in SDN-based mobile networks.
back: It is an agent-based solution where an 'Odin agent' is placed at access points to communicate with an 'Odin master' at the controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What are the two main parts of the UbiFlow solution?
back: Mobility management and flow scheduling.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What aspects does UbiFlow's mobility management address?
back: Scalable control of access points and fault tolerance.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: Explain the three components of UbiFlow's flow scheduling.
back: Network partitioning (fragmenting the network into multiple partitions), network matching (checking which partition should handle a packet), and load balancing (distributing load evenly across partitions).

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What is the primary goal of MobiFlow?
back: To provide mobility-aware flow rule placement for mobile-based IoT systems.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: How does MobiFlow achieve proactive rule placement?
back: By predicting the location of the end-users at the next time instant based on their movement history.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What technique does MobiFlow use for location prediction?
back: The order K Markov predictor, which takes the last K location instances to predict the next location.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What method does MobiFlow use for optimal access point selection for flow rule placement?
back: A linear programming-based solution.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What are the main benefits of MobiFlow compared to conventional rule placement schemes?
back: Minimized control message overhead and reduced energy consumption.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: How are rule placement schemes handled for the backbone network in SDN-based IoT?
back: Existing rule placement schemes for wired networks can be used, as backbone networks often have similar topology and architecture.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What is an important issue in backbone networks due to the dynamic nature of IoT, and what can be integrated to address it?
back: Load balancing is an important issue, and dynamic resource allocation can be integrated.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: In data center networks with SDN, what are the two types of flows observed?
back: Mice flows (small, short-lived) and Elephant flows (large, long-lived).

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: How are 'mice flows' typically handled in SDN-based data center networks?
back: Wildcard rules can be placed to deal with these flows.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: How are 'elephant flows' typically handled in SDN-based data center networks?
back: Exact match of the rules is required.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What is a prerequisite for inserting flow rules at switches to adequately forward data in SDN-based data center networks?
back: Classifying the flows (as mice or elephant) before inserting the flow rules.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: How can anomaly detection be performed in an IoT network using SDN/OpenFlow?
back: By monitoring each flow in the network or by collecting different port statistics at the different switches.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: Name an experimental platform that supports both wired and wireless networks for SDN-based IoT.
back: Mininet-WiFi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What protocols does Mininet-WiFi support for wired and wireless networks?
back: Ethernet protocol for wired and the 802.11 class of protocols for wireless.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: Which platform is mentioned for helping with controller placement in SDN-based IoT?
back: The ONOS platform.

lectureTitle: Lecture 36 : Software Defined IoT Networking- II
front: What are the three specific SDN solutions mentioned for mobile IoT networks in this lecture?
back: ODIN, UbiFlow, and MobiFlow.

front: What is the fundamental concept behind cloud computing, analogous to utilities like electricity or water?
back: Computing as a utility.

front: How does cloud computing address the need for infrastructure deployment, similar to how electricity or water utilities work?
back: Users do not need to deploy the necessary infrastructure; they subscribe and pay for usage.

front: What are the three main types of resources considered 'computing' in the context of 'computing as a utility'?
back: Hardware resources (servers, workstations, processors, memory, storage), software resources, and development platforms.

front: List the evolutionary stages of computing that led to cloud computing.
back: Cluster computing, Grid computing, Utility computing, Cloud computing.

front: What is the primary characteristic of 'cluster computing'?
back: Having some kind of computing nodes connected together in the form of a cluster to accomplish some computational job.

front: According to NIST, what is cloud computing defined as?
back: A model for enabling convenient on-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources (e.g., network, infrastructure, servers, storage, applications).

front: Name the five essential characteristics of cloud computing.
back: Broad network access, Rapid elasticity, Measured services, On-demand self-service, Resource pooling.

front: Explain 'Broad network access' as an essential characteristic of cloud computing.
back: Cloud resources should be available over the network (e.g., internet) and support standard mechanisms for information retrieval using traditional interfaces (e.g., thick clients, thin clients, mobile phones, laptops).

front: What does 'Rapid elasticity' in cloud computing refer to?
back: Cloud resource allocations should be rapid, elastic, and automatic, allowing dynamic allocation and release of facilities for scaling in and scaling out of resources.

front: How are 'Measured services' implemented in cloud computing?
back: Resources and their uses would be recorded and monitored, and the cloud service provider sends a bill to the end user based on units of usage.

front: Describe 'On-demand self-service' in the context of cloud computing.
back: Whenever required, the user should be able to get access to these resources through a self-service manner, with the cloud providing server time and network storage automatically.

front: What is 'Resource pooling' in cloud computing?
back: A multi-tenancy model where multiple end users share available resources, which are automatically made available and pooled from all available sources, allocated according to user demand.

front: List three business advantages of using cloud computing.
back: Without any upfront infrastructure investment, real-time infrastructure availability, more efficient resource utilization, usage-based costing, reduced time to market, improved agility.

front: What is 'Multitenancy' in cloud computing?
back: Sharing of resources and costs across a large pool of users.

front: What are the four main components of cloud computing from a user's perspective?
back: Clients (thin, thick, mobile), Services (web apps, platforms), Storage (databases, data storage), Infrastructure (virtualized).

front: Name the three most popular cloud service models.
back: Software as a Service (SaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS).

front: What does 'Software as a Service (SaaS)' provide to users?
back: Facility to execute service providers' applications at the users' end, with applications available as services accessed via different types of client devices (e.g., web browsers, apps).

front: Give two commercial examples of Software as a Service (SaaS).
back: Google Apps, Salesforce, Learn.com.

front: What does 'Platform as a Service (PaaS)' offer to consumers?
back: The development platform is made available to the consumers as facilities to execute consumer-created and acquired applications onto the cloud infrastructure.

front: Provide two commercial examples of Platform as a Service (PaaS).
back: Windows Azure, Google App Engine.

front: What does 'Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)' entail?
back: Most computing infrastructure like network, storage, operating system to be made available as facilities through the internet, accessing these facilities as computational resources dynamically on a pay-per-use basis.

front: Name two commercial examples of Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS).
back: Amazon EC2, GoGrid, Iland, Rackspace Cloud Servers.

front: List the four main cloud deployment models discussed.
back: Public cloud, Private cloud, Hybrid cloud, Community cloud.

front: Describe a 'Public Cloud' and give an example.
back: Set up for the use of any person or industry, typically owned by an organization who offers the cloud service. Examples: Amazon Web Services, Google Compute Engine, Microsoft Azure.

front: What is a 'Private Cloud' and what is its primary advantage?
back: Typically restricted to a single organization, with cloud functionalities made available only within the organization. Advantage: Total control over the system and the data.

front: What is a 'Hybrid Cloud'?
back: Combines the facilities of two or more types of unique cloud types (e.g., private, community, or public cloud), pooling resources from different infrastructures.

front: What defines a 'Community Cloud'?
back: Typically restricted to certain communities (e.g., medical community, hospital community, security community), where only the users of that community can access its services.

front: What is the key difference in resource sharing between a public cloud and a private cloud?
back: In public cloud, resources are publicly shared (multiple customers), while in private cloud, resources are privately shared (few customers, typically users of the organization).

front: What is an 'Inter-Cloud'?
back: A 'cloud of clouds' where multiple different clouds are put together, unified through the internet, and interoperate between each other to offer joint cloud services to users.

front: Why is cloud computing considered an important enabling technology for the Internet of Things (IoT)?
back: It helps deal with heterogeneous resources and data, enables fast processing without much infrastructure involvement, and offers computing facilities on a pay-per-use model.

front: What are the three core service models in cloud computing?
back: Software as a Service (SaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS).

front: According to Amazon, what does Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) contain?
back: The basic building blocks for cloud IT, typically providing access to networking features, computers (virtual or dedicated hardware), and data storage space.

front: What is the primary benefit of Platform as a Service (PaaS) for organizations?
back: It removes the need for organizations to manage the underlying infrastructure (hardware and OS), allowing focus on application deployment and management.

front: How does Amazon define Software as a Service (SaaS)?
back: SaaS provides a completed product that is run and managed by the service provider, typically referring to end-user applications.

front: Name four features provided by Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS).
back: Servers (for computation), Storage, Network, Operating System.

front: In a virtualized server model for IaaS, what manages the interaction between the hardware layer and the VM layer?
back: Hypervisor.

front: How does IaaS benefit new businesses?
back: New businesses can kickstart without having to invest in computing hardware.

front: Give an example of a business scenario where IaaS is suitable due to fluctuating computing demands.
back: Businesses like Flipkart or Amazon during festive seasons, needing more infrastructure temporarily.

front: What is a key advantage of IaaS regarding resource allocation?
back: Dynamic scaling of required infrastructure resources, allowing large allocation or release in a short span of time without performance variation.

front: What level of control do clients have over virtualized infrastructure resources in IaaS?
back: Total control, allowing them to preconfigure facilities, virtualize resources, and monitor their running status.

front: Name one challenge or limitation of Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) related to compliance.
back: Regulatory approval may be required for outsourced storage and processing.

front: How might network conditions impact IaaS performance?
back: Network latency may degrade the level of expected performance.

front: What is the primary role of Platform as a Service (PaaS) for developers?
back: It provides the platform which allows developers to create applications that can be offered as services via the internet.

front: What two key aspects does PaaS provide for developed applications?
back: Abstraction and security.

front: Name three features of PaaS that support application development.
back: Server-side scripting, database management, and offering different tools for design and development of software.

front: How does PaaS support users in creating software applications?
back: It allows users to create software applications using offered tools and provides pre-configured features that customers can subscribe to.

front: What is a business advantage of PaaS related to development tools?
back: Easy access to development and deployment tools, and freedom from managing them individually.

front: Who is the typical user of Software as a Service (SaaS)?
back: End-user applications.

front: How is SaaS typically accessed, and what acts as the client?
back: Over the internet, using a web browser as a thin client.

front: What kind of pricing model does SaaS typically support?
back: A fully pay-as-you-go model.

front: What is multi-tenancy in the context of SaaS?
back: The ability to accommodate users from multiple companies at the same time, an architectural shift from isolated single-tenant applications.

front: Compare traditional software and SaaS regarding installation and maintenance.
back: Traditional: Customers install, manage, and maintain. SaaS: Customers simply use over the internet.

front: What is the difference between traditional software and SaaS concerning cross-platform support?
back: Traditional software requires cross-platform support; SaaS has no concern for it.

front: What is a limitation of SaaS regarding control?
back: Supporting centralized control.

front: What is a limitation of SaaS related to adaptability?
back: Limited flexibility.

front: What are key concerns regarding data in the SaaS model?
back: Data security and privacy concerns.

front: In traditional computing, who manages the Operating System? How about in IaaS?
back: Traditional: User manages OS. IaaS: User manages OS (service provider manages virtualization, server, storage, networking).

front: In IaaS, who manages the Operating System? How about in PaaS?
back: IaaS: User manages OS. PaaS: Service provider manages OS (user only manages applications and data).

front: In PaaS, who manages applications and data? How about in SaaS?
back: PaaS: User manages applications and data. SaaS: Service provider manages everything (including applications and data).

front: What are the three deployment models for IaaS?
back: Public cloud, private cloud, and hybrid cloud.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What is the primary focus of this lecture series on cloud computing for IoT?
back: Service management and security issues in cloud computing for IoT.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What is the aim of service management in cloud computing?
back: To provide equal importance to desired outcomes of customers through optimal performance, ensuring satisfaction with minimum risk and no extra cost.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Give an example of risk mitigation in cloud service management.
back: If a computing resource becomes unavailable, a risk mitigation technique should dynamically provision an additional physical resource mapped to the virtual one the customer was using, without the customer noticing.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: List three types of services that should be offered in cloud computing.
back: Usage monitoring and billing, clear service description, high availability of networks and connectivity, ease of access, service selection portals, service guarantees, rapid fulfillment/decommissioning, secure environment.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Define Service Level Agreement (SLA) in cloud computing.
back: A non-functional requirement expected from the cloud service provider, acting as a roadmap with clearly defined deliverables, describing the quality, utility, and warranty of services.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What are the three core components used for billing in cloud computing?
back: Accounting records (tracking resource use), resource prices (unit cost), and billing rules (policy for billing based on consumption).

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: How does hardware differ between traditional data centers and cloud computing?
back: Traditional data centers use heterogeneous hardware with network computing and remote servers. Cloud computing uses off-premise resources with virtually hosted solutions, heterogeneous hardware, software, and networks available on the cloud.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Name two differences between traditional IT infrastructure and cloud computing, besides hardware.
back: Resilience and elasticity, flexibility and scalability, automation, running costs (cloud has running costs vs. one-time/periodic), security (cloud has more security).

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What does 'resilience' mean in the context of cloud resources?
back: The ability of the system to handle failures or issues without the users noticing, taking care of problems in the background.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: List the four customer population metrics that influence the economics of scaling in cloud computing.
back: Number of unique customer sets, duty cycle of the customer set, relative displacement duty cycle, and load of the customer set.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Provide three economic incentives for using cloud computing.
back: Lowering infrastructure and computing costs, CapEx-free computing, faster project deployment fostering innovation, scaling up/down as required, lower maintenance costs, resiliency and redundancy.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What are the key demands of a cloud database management system (DBMS)?
back: Efficiency, fault tolerance, adaptivity to heterogeneity, operational comfort on encrypted data, and the ability to interface with different products and solutions.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Name two Database as a Service (DBaaS) platforms mentioned for cloud integration.
back: Microsoft Azure SQL Database, Amazon Web Services (DynamoDB, Relational Database Service), Google Cloud SQL, Google App Engine Data Store, ClearDB, Database.com.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Why is data security particularly important in cloud computing?
back: Data is stored on geographically distributed servers and platforms, often without the user knowing its physical location, leading to a loss of control over information on the public cloud.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: List three specific concerns regarding security in a cloud platform.
back: Loss of data, seizing of the account, service traffic hindrance, vulnerability of APIs.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What is the general solution to cloud security issues?
back: Implementing counter security solutions, platforms, APIs, and software to protect from theft, leakage, or accidental deletion of data by providing security policies.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What are the three main levels of infrastructure security in cloud computing?
back: Network level security, Host level security, and Application level security.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What are the network-level security concerns for data in transit to and from a cloud service provider?
back: Achieving confidentiality and integrity of data in transit.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What is the 'Blue Pill attack' and which cloud component does it target?
back: A specific type of attack on the hypervisor, which is a core component of IaaS platforms, tasked with managing virtual machines.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Who is responsible for application-level security in a SaaS model?
back: The SaaS cloud service provider is primarily responsible for the security of deliverable applications.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Who is responsible for application-level security in an IaaS model?
back: The IaaS customer is responsible for arranging their own security mechanisms for applications.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What are the three primary objectives of data security?
back: Confidentiality (data available only to intended stakeholders), Integrity (data not tampered with), and Availability (data available as per SLA).

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Define 'data at rest' in the context of data security.
back: Data that is used for long-term use, doesn't change fast, and will be stored in the server for future use.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What is the purpose of Identity and Access Management (IAM) in cloud security?
back: To allow legitimate persons to retrieve legitimate resources at legitimate times for legitimate reasons.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What does an IAM module instigate, administer, and record?
back: User identities and access permissions.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Name three features of an Identity and Access Management (IAM) module.
back: Single access control interface, increased security, access control over resource level, improvement of operational efficiency, organizations attaining access control and operation security, improvement of regulatory compliance management.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: List three access control layers in the cloud.
back: Cloud access, server level access, service level access, database access (direct/indirect), VM access, access to objects within a virtual machine.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Differentiate between 'trust' and 'reputation' in cloud computing.
back: Trust is the independent expectancy between two entities for a specific context at a given time. Reputation is the belief of an entity's standing in the community.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: Name two modes of trust establishment for customers selecting a cloud provider.
back: Accomplishment of Service Level Agreements (SLAs), application of audit standards, measuring and rating, questionnaires for self-assessment.

lectureTitle: Lecture 39 : Cloud Computing-Service Management and Security
front: What is a consequence of a threat to the user authentication process in the cloud?
back: It can lead to the divulging of confidential data to a fake user.

front: What are the key reasons to use cloud simulation platforms before actual deployment?
back: To assess technology, evaluate different solutions, understand performance implications, and study new features.

front: What three core qualities must cloud simulation tools ensure for performance evaluation?
back: Reliability, scalability, and repeatability.

front: Name three purposes of cloud simulators.
back: Facilitate pre-deployment tests, study how new features perform, and allow customers to evaluate services at no additional cost.

front: List at least three cloud simulation platforms mentioned.
back: CloudSim, CloudAnalyst, GreenCloud, iCanCloud, GroudSim, DCSim.

front: What programming language is CloudSim based on?
back: Java.

front: Who developed CloudSim and at which university?
back: Professor Rajkumar Buyya's team at the University of Melbourne.

front: Name two advantages of using CloudSim.
back: Time effectiveness and flexibility/applicability (supporting diverse cloud environments).

front: Describe the three main layers of CloudSim's architecture.
back: User code layer (machine/app specs), CloudSim layer (cloud environment modeling), and Core engine layer (event scheduling, entity creation, clock management).

front: What is a 'cloudlet' in CloudSim's user interface structure?
back: A small physical server which creates virtual machines.

front: List two types of modules/models available in CloudSim for cloud computing environments.
back: Modules for data centers, virtual machines, applications, users, or network topology.

front: What does the Core Engine layer in CloudSim's architecture primarily handle?
back: Event scheduling, entity creation, component interaction, and clock management.

front: What is CloudAnalyst built on top of?
back: CloudSim.

front: What is the primary purpose of CloudAnalyst?
back: To study the behavior of geographically distributed large-scale cloud applications under different deployment configurations.

front: Name two features that make CloudAnalyst user-friendly and powerful.
back: Easy to use (due to GUI) and high level of configurability.

front: What are the two main components of the CloudAnalyst architecture?
back: CloudSim extensions (for metrics) and the Graphical User Interface (GUI).

front: What is the primary focus of the GreenCloud simulator?
back: Energy awareness and monitoring energy consumption in cloud data centers.

front: GreenCloud was developed as an extension of which existing network simulator?
back: ns-2 (packet-level network simulator).

front: Name two features of GreenCloud that highlight its purpose.
back: Monitors energy consumption of network and devices, and enables improved power management schemes.

front: Name two open-source cloud platforms.
back: OpenStack, CloudStack, or Eucalyptus.

front: Name two commercial cloud platforms.
back: Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, or Google App Engine.

front: What is a key difference in security implementation between open-source and commercial cloud platforms?
back: Open-source: security implemented by the user. Commercial: security implemented by the service provider.

front: What type of cloud deployment is typical for open-source cloud platforms?
back: Private on-premise.

front: Which service model does OpenStack primarily support?
back: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS).

front: What is OpenStack managed by?
back: The OpenStack Foundation.

front: Name two core components of OpenStack and their functions.
back: Nova (compute) and Neutron (networking).

front: What two primary service models does Microsoft Azure support?
back: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and Platform as a Service (PaaS).

front: What is a key benefit of Azure's PaaS offering for clients?
back: Clients can focus on application development rather than worrying about hardware and infrastructure.

front: Name two types of services offered by Microsoft Azure.
back: Computing services and storage services.

front: What does EC2 stand for in Amazon EC2?
back: Elastic Compute Cloud.

front: How does Amazon EC2 handle persistent storage?
back: Through Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) and Simple Storage Service (S3).

front: What is OpenStack?
back: An open-source software platform for generating your own cloud, a joint project of NASA and Rackspace Hosting.

front: When was OpenStack first released?
Name some major companies contributing to OpenStack development.
back: Cisco, IBM, HP, Red Hat.

front: What is unique about OpenStack compared to other cloud developing software?
back: It is completely free and the only completely free open-source cloud developing software available.

front: How are OpenStack versions named?
back: In alphabetical order.

front: What is the function of Horizon in OpenStack?
back: It is the GUI interface/dashboard section, providing an overview of other components.

front: Which OpenStack component handles authentication and authorization?
back: Keystone.

front: What is Nova's role in OpenStack?
back: It is the compute service, used for launching virtual machine instances.

front: What is Glance used for in OpenStack?
back: It is the image service, used for discovering, registering, and retrieving VM images, and creating snapshots.

front: Which OpenStack component provides full object storage?
back: Swift.

front: What is the primary function of Neutron in OpenStack?
back: It is the networking part of the system, providing networking services and allowing users to create and modify networks (Network as a Service).

front: What type of storage does Cinder provide in OpenStack?
back: Block storage (pluggable type).

front: Which OpenStack component provides orchestration?
back: Heat.

front: What is the purpose of Ceilometer in OpenStack?
back: It is the billing section, used to monitor resource usage (what, how long) for cloud service providers.

front: What is DevStack used for in OpenStack?
back: A script-based method for easily installing OpenStack, where installation steps are pre-written.

front: What command is used to install OpenStack using DevStack?
back: `stack.sh`

front: What command is used to uninstall OpenStack using DevStack?
back: `unstack.sh`

front: What is the first step shown in the practical demonstration for launching an instance?
back: Creating a key pair.

front: Why is a key pair required when launching an OpenStack instance?
back: For authentication and authorization to access the instance.
